methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json or quarterly/<YEAR>_Q<N>.json (Q1-Q3 unaudited interim quarters added 2026-08-27, Q4/annual quarters generated 2026-08-26). All cited figures were verified programmatically against those files before this document was finalized.

risk_signals.statement: Union Bank's FY2023 annual report was audited under a CLEAN, UNQUALIFIED opinion (M M Rahman & Co., signed 25 April 2024), reporting Shareholders' Equity of BDT 16,337.89m, CRAR of 11.11%, classified investments of BDT 9,263.05m (3.62% of gross investments), and Net Profit after Tax of BDT 1,607.89m. Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report -- audited a year later by a different firm (Syful Shamsul Alam & Co.) under a QUALIFIED opinion -- restates the identical FY2023 balance-sheet date to Shareholders' Equity BDT 11,884.45m, CRAR -18.81%, classified investments BDT 106,510.90m (41.66% of gross investments, an over 11-fold increase), and a NET LOSS of BDT -2,875.22m. The FY2024 report's own Qualified Opinion attributes this to 'System-generated reports on classified investments... manipulated in breach of IT protocols' and BDT 1,962.72 crore of income 'inappropriately recognized... which subsequently been reversed' per Bangladesh Bank letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347 (29 April 2025). This dataset stores the original, contemporaneous FY2023 figures per project methodology (see 2023_Q4.json's period_note and sources.json for the full restatement finding and independent press corroboration).

FY2024 net loss was BDT -257,936.69m -- independently corroborated by Bangladesh press (The Daily Star) reporting a 'Tk 25,790cr' loss, described as 'the biggest loss in [Bangladesh] banking history'. Shareholders' Equity swung from +BDT 16,337.89m (FY2023, originally reported) to -BDT 246,052.24m (FY2024) -- a single-year negative swing of over BDT 262 billion (262,390.13m), or about 16x the bank's entire FY2023 capital base. Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) fell to -405.31% (Total Regulatory Capital BDT -244,147.33m against Total Risk-Weighted Assets of BDT 60,237.66m), by far the most extreme CRAR reading in this dataset. Classified investments reached BDT 269,702.99m, i.e. 95.34% of gross investments of BDT 282,874.56m -- meaning fewer than 1 in 20 Taka of the bank's investment book was performing at year-end.

Newly-sourced Q1-Q3 2024 unaudited interim filings (added 2026-08-27) show Union Bank was still solvent and only mildly stressed as of 30 September 2024: Total Shareholders' Equity was BDT +15,964.45m (positive), 9-month cumulative Net Profit after Tax was BDT +147.66m (positive, though down sharply from BDT +949.47m at the June-2024 half-year point because of a discrete Q3-2024-alone LOSS of BDT -801.81m -- the first negative quarter in this bank's entire recorded interim series), and 9-month cumulative Total Provisions were BDT 1,550.50m (of which BDT 1,040.0m was booked in Q3 alone, roughly 4x the prior quarter and 9-14x every earlier quarter in the series). Combining these interim figures with this dataset's existing FY2024 annual figures (2024_Q4.json) shows the entire remainder of the year's damage landed in a single quarter: Q4-2024-ALONE net loss = -257,936.69m (FY total) minus +147.66m (9-month cumulative) = approximately -258,084.35m; Q4-2024-ALONE Total Provisions = 238,884.46m (FY total) minus 1,550.50m (9-month cumulative) = approximately 237,333.96m, i.e. about 153 times the combined first nine months; Q4-2024-ALONE equity swing = -246,052.24m (FY-end) minus +15,964.45m (30-Sept-2024) = approximately -262,016.69m. In other words, over 99.9% of the largest single-bank annual loss in Bangladeshi banking history was recognised in one unaudited-to-audited transition at year-end, not progressively through the year's own quarterly disclosures -- the interim filings gave real but comparatively modest warning (a single quarter's ~800m loss against a ~16 billion capital base) before the ~262 billion wipeout was booked.

Every one of Union Bank's own 2024 Q1, Q2 and Q3 unaudited interim filings (dated 25 April 2024, 30 July 2024 and 31 October 2024 respectively) reproduces its 'December 2023' comparative balance sheet column EXACTLY matching this dataset's stored ORIGINAL/contemporaneous FY2023 figures (Total Assets 295,347,564,528; Total Liabilities 279,009,675,195; Total Shareholders' Equity 16,337,889,333) -- NOT the figures Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report would later restate them to (Total Equity 11,884.45m, a loss of -2,875.22m instead of the originally-reported +1,607.89m profit). This is direct, dated proof that the classified-investment-data manipulation Bangladesh Bank found (letter DBI-7/4(4)/2025-347, dated 29 April 2025) had not yet been detected or reflected anywhere in Union Bank's own published numbers as late as 31 October 2024 -- over 22 months after the FY2023 year-end it concerns, and only about 6 months before the finding was made. Separately, every one of Union Bank's 2023 Q1/Q2/Q3 interim filings itself shows a smoothly IMPROVING trajectory throughout the year (cumulative Net Profit after Tax growing 353.90m to 839.47m to 1,367.50m; equity growing 15,627.12m to 15,584.84m to 16,102.31m) with no visible sign of trouble, consistent with the FY2023 annual report's own clean, unqualified audit opinion (M M Rahman & Co., signed 25 April 2024). This dataset's Q1-Q3 backfill therefore cannot identify any point at which the manipulation became visible in Union Bank's own published interim numbers before the FY2024 annual audit itself -- only that it was not visible in nine consecutive quarterly filings spanning January 2023 through September 2024.

The preceding finding was independently re-derived in a follow-up session (2026-08-28) by reading the raw OCR'd text of all three 2024 interim filings directly (annual_reports/UNIONBANK/unionbank-unaudited-2024-q1.txt, -q2.txt, -q3.txt), rather than relying on the prior session's summary. Each filing's own 'December 2023' comparative column, read verbatim, is IDENTICAL across all three and matches this dataset's stored ORIGINAL FY2023 values exactly -- Total Assets 295,347,564,528 and Total Shareholders' Equity 16,337,889,333 -- in the Q1 filing (as at 31 March 2024, signed 25 April 2024), the Q2 filing (as at 30 June 2024, signed 30 July 2024), and the Q3 filing (as at 30 September 2024, signed 31 October 2024) alike; none show the later-restated figures (equity 11,884.45m). This confirms, directly from primary-source line items rather than a derived summary, that Union Bank's own published books had genuinely not been restated as late as 31 October 2024, the latest-dated of the three filings and six months before Bangladesh Bank's manipulated-data finding letter (29 April 2025).

Union Bank's FY2024 Qualified Audit Opinion discloses that 74.20% of the bank's total Investment portfolio (BDT 20,989.72 crore / BDT 209,897.2m) was concentrated in a single borrower group, confirmed by Bangladesh Bank at a triparty meeting dated 23 April 2025 -- breaching the 15%-of-capital regulatory concentration ceiling under Section 26(B) of the Bank Company Act 1991 (as amended 2023) by a factor of roughly 5x. The auditor's report states this group meets the IAS 24 definition of a related party, yet Note 43 'Related Party Transactions' stated the Bank had no related-party transactions during the year -- a disclosure gap the auditors flagged directly. This concentration pattern is consistent with the broader S. Alam Group-linked bank resolution program documented elsewhere in this dataset (EXIMBANK's own FY2024 report explicitly names 'S Alam Group' related-party lending concentrations as its precipitating issue; this dataset's cross-bank research memo describes the five-bank Sammilito Islami Bank merger as resolving 'S Alam Group-linked banks' generally), though Union Bank's own FY2024 report does not itself name the group, and SIBL had not yet been examined in this dataset as of this writing.

Union Bank's Investment Deposit Ratio (IDR) exceeded 99% from FY2022 onward and breached 100% in FY2023 -- 99.64% (FY2022) and 108.50% (FY2023, originally reported, i.e. under the still-clean audit opinion) -- already far above the 92% regulatory ceiling that the FY2024 Qualified Audit Opinion later cites explicitly (IDR 115.63% in FY2024 'exceeding the regulatory ceiling of 92% prescribed by DOS Circular No. 02 dated 12 April 2020'). This means the liquidity-stress warning sign was visible in Union Bank's own published, audited numbers at least one full year (FY2023) before the auditors' qualification made it explicit -- IDR moved through 88.34% (FY2017), 96.03% (FY2018), 92.48% (FY2019), 90.22% (FY2020) and 91.55% (FY2021) before climbing to 99.64% (FY2022) and 108.50% (FY2023).

Classified investments as a percentage of gross investments rose steadily and continuously from 0.07% (FY2016) to 0.57% (FY2017) to 0.97% (FY2018) to 3.64% (FY2019) -- a greater-than-50x increase in three years, albeit from a very low base -- before plateauing in a 2.53%-3.62% band from FY2020 through FY2023 (originally reported). This multi-year, unbroken upward trend from a near-zero starting point through FY2019 was an early, visible signal of underwriting/asset-quality weakness years before the FY2024 collapse, even though the absolute levels through FY2023 (as originally reported) remained low by sector standards.

Union Bank's Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) started very high in its founding year (34.46% in FY2013, reflecting a small, newly-capitalized balance sheet) and declined steadily as the balance sheet scaled: 14.31% (FY2014), 13.27% (FY2015), 11.62% (FY2016), settling in an 10.24%-12.24% band from FY2017 through FY2023 (originally reported) -- consistently above the 10%-of-RWA minimum disclosed in the bank's own capital-adequacy notes throughout, but with little buffer above it in most years, leaving limited room to absorb the shock that materialized in FY2024.

Union Bank's FY2024 Balance Sheet is signed by a 'Deputy Managing Director', an 'Associate of Administrator' and an 'Administrator' -- rather than the Managing Director/Directors/Chairman panel that signed every prior year's balance sheet (FY2013-2023) -- confirming Bangladesh Bank had already placed the bank under administration before the FY2024 audit (signed 13 November 2025, ~10.5 months after fiscal year-end) was completed. The same report's going-concern paragraph discloses that 'on October 9, 2025, the Advisory Council of the Interim Government of Bangladesh approved the merger of this bank with other four banks... to form a new state-owned Islamic bank' -- i.e. the resolution process was already underway before the FY2024 annual report itself was finalized.

Union Bank never published a standalone FY2025 annual report and is very unlikely ever to. It was one of five distressed Shariah-based banks (with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank) merged by Bangladesh Bank into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, as part of the resolution of S. Alam Group-linked banks. Bangladesh Bank declared Union Bank 'non-viable' under Section 15 of the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, effective 5 November 2025 (the same date DSE suspended trading in its shares), and per independent press reporting shareholders of all five banks will receive no shares in the merged entity because the value of assets tied to their existing shareholding is already negative -- consistent with this dataset's own finding of BDT -246,052.24m shareholders' equity at FY2024 year-end. This is very likely a permanent series-end for Union Bank as a standalone reporting entity: any future consolidated figures for this business would appear, if at all, under Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, a distinct legal entity outside this dataset's scope.

historical_context: Union Bank PLC is one of Bangladesh's youngest listed banks: incorporated 07 March 2013 as a Shariah-based Islamic bank from day one (unlike GIB, which converted from conventional banking mid-series), it grew its balance sheet from BDT 17,081.14m (partial-year FY2013) to BDT 295,347.56m (FY2023) over a decade -- a roughly 17-fold increase -- funded by rapid deposit growth (BDT 12,165.20m to BDT 225,585.37m) and completing an IPO/DSE listing in January 2022 that raised paid-up capital by about 77% (BDT 5,589.34m to BDT 9,869.34m). Profitability was consistently positive throughout FY2013-2023 (originally reported), with ROE (period-end equity basis) ranging from a first-year 1.94% up to a peak of 14.13% (FY2016) and settling in a 7.03%-10.80% band from FY2019-2023, and CRAR remaining above the bank's own 10%-of-RWA disclosed minimum throughout, albeit on a generally declining trend from a founding-year high of 34.46%. Classified investments crept up from a near-zero base (0.07% in FY2016) to 3.64% by FY2019, then plateaued in a 2.5%-3.6% band through FY2023 as originally reported -- a slow-burning asset-quality signal that, together with an Investment-Deposit Ratio that climbed past 99% (FY2022) and then 108% (FY2023), pointed toward mounting balance-sheet stress even under a still-clean audit opinion. The full scale of that stress was revealed only retrospectively: Union Bank's own FY2024 annual report shows its FY2023 comparative figures were built on 'manipulated' classified-investment system reports and improperly recognized income (per a Bangladesh Bank finding dated 29 April 2025), restating FY2023 from a BDT 1,607.89m profit and 11.11% CRAR to a BDT -2,875.22m loss and -18.81% CRAR. FY2024 itself was a full-blown collapse: a BDT -257,936.69m net loss (independently reported by Bangladesh media as the largest annual loss in the country's banking history), shareholders' equity of BDT -246,052.24m, CRAR of -405.31%, classified investments of 95.34% of gross investments, and a Qualified Audit Opinion documenting a 74.20%-of-portfolio single-borrower concentration, branch-level fraud findings, breached liquidity and capital-adequacy ratios, and a going-concern paragraph disclosing that Bangladesh Bank had already approved (9 October 2025) a merger of Union Bank with four other distressed Shariah-based banks -- EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank and Social Islami Bank -- into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC. Bangladesh Bank formally declared Union Bank 'non-viable' effective 5 November 2025 and DSE suspended its share trading the same date; this dataset's Union Bank series therefore most likely ends at FY2024, with FY2024 standing as the bank's terminal standalone financial statement, and its equity holders receiving nothing in the resolution.
data_gaps: Q4/year-end (audited) data spans FY2013 (partial, ~10-month first period) through FY2024. Q1/Q2/Q3 unaudited interim data (added 2026-08-27) is available for FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 (9 quarters total) -- sourced from the bank's own 'Quarterly Statement' investor-relations page, which itself has no filing earlier than Q1 2022; a broad Wayback CDX sweep found no evidence any FY2013-2021 interim filing was ever published, plausibly because Union Bank only began publishing quarterly statements publicly around its January-2022 DSE listing (see sources.json) -- FY2013-2021 Q1-Q3 is therefore treated as a likely-genuine non-existence, not backfilled. Every 2022-2024 interim filing's balance-sheet identity and full P&L chain (Operating Income - Expenses = Operating Profit; - Provisions = PBT; - Tax = PAT) reconciles exactly to the Taka; small (<0.02 BDT-million, i.e. <0.002%) rounding-only differences appear when re-summing the *rounded* (2-decimal, BDT-million) figures stored in quarterly/*.json, an artifact of rounding several independently-derived line items rather than a data error -- the underlying raw-Taka source figures were verified with zero tolerance before rounding. Two of the nine interim filings (2022 Q1, 2023 Q1) were genuine text-layer PDFs extracted with pdftotext; the other seven were scanned-image PDFs independently OCR'd (pdftoppm + tesseract), cross-validated by the arithmetic reconciliation above and, where available, by an adjacent quarter's own reproduced comparative column. None of the nine interim filings disclose classified investments, NPL ratio, or CRAR/capital-adequacy figures -- these remain Q4/annual-only for this bank, unlike the flow figures (profit, provisioning) which are now visible quarterly for 2022-2024. FY2025 does not exist and is very unlikely to ever be published for Union Bank as a standalone entity -- confirmed via a time-boxed, multi-source check on 2026-08-26 (a Wayback CDX pass over the bank's own website found no FY2025-named filing and exposed a stale, misleadingly generic 'latest annual report' link that actually still points to the FY2021 report; the bank's own FY2024 report discloses the merger approval directly; and independent press confirms the non-viable declaration, trading suspension, and merger into Sammilito Islami Bank PLC) -- see sources.json and the merger_into_sammilito_islami_bank_series_end risk signal for the full finding. Several years' decorative 'Financial Performance at a Glance' / 'Annexure B Financial Highlights' summary pages (FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, and FY2024) extracted as badly garbled or entirely blank text in this archive despite the surrounding core financial statements (Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, capital-adequacy notes) extracting cleanly; for those years, every figure in this dataset was instead sourced directly from the clean core statements and independently cross-checked against an adjacent year's comparative column (see each year's period_note and sources.json for the specific reconciliation). ldr_pct is available for every year FY2013-2023 (not FY2024, whose Annexure B was unreadable -- though the auditor's report separately quotes FY2024's IDR at 115.63%, recorded in 2024_Q4.json's period_note but not as a structured field since it was not independently cross-checked). roa_pct is available for FY2013 and FY2015-2023 but not FY2014 (the one year whose own summary page was both garbled AND not independently reproduced in an adjacent report's comparative column). cost_of_fund_pct is available only for FY2017-2023 (not FY2013-2016, whose own summary pages did not yield this field even after cross-referencing adjacent reports). nav_per_share is available only for FY2023 (reported) and FY2024 (calculated as total_equity/shares outstanding, since equity is negative that year) -- not a uniform gap but a reflection of which fields each year's own summary tables actually disclosed and which of those pages extracted legibly. A small number of cross-report figure discrepancies in the low single-digit-percent-or-smaller range were found and are documented in each affected year's period_note and in sources.json rather than silently reconciled (FY2015 total assets/liabilities ~0.018%, FY2018 Investment Deposit Ratio ~3.07pp / provision-kept ~0.86%, FY2019 total assets/liabilities ~0.046% and cost-of-fund ~3pp, FY2016 capital-adequacy presentation ~0.34%/0.04pp, FY2021 total assets/liabilities ~2.4%) -- all far smaller in both scale and consequence than the FY2023 restatement, which is the dataset's central finding for this bank. A follow-up session (2026-08-28) independently re-confirmed the FY2013-2021 Q1-Q3 non-existence via a full-domain (not keyword-filtered) Wayback CDX sweep of unionbank.com.bd covering all 3,630 of the domain's captures and manually reviewing every pre-2022-listing PDF found -- see sources.json for the detailed method and the newly-checked /psinformation/ disclosure-notice folder (itself only starting 2022-08-17, further corroborating the no-obligation-before-listing explanation). That session also independently re-verified, by reading the raw OCR'd source text of the 2024 Q1/Q2/Q3 filings directly rather than trusting the prior summary, that every one of their 'December 2023' comparative columns matches this dataset's stored original FY2023 figures exactly (see the corresponding risk_signal above). No new quarters were added; the 9-quarter (2022-2024) Q1-Q3 series remains this bank's ceiling absent a structural change (e.g. discovery of a pre-2022 private-placement disclosure), which this session judged unlikely enough not to be worth further chasing given the bank's series-end status.
